title: 2024 AMC 10A Problem 11
statement:
How many ordered pairs of integers \((m, n)\) satisfy

\[\sqrt{n^2 - 49} = m?\]

solutions.text: Note \(m = \sqrt{n^2 - 49} \ge 0\) has to be an integer, so \(n^2 - 49 = m^2,\) which means \((n - m)(n + m) = 49.\) The factorizations of \(49\) give \(|n| = 25, m = 24\) or \(|n| = 7, m = 0.\) So the ordered pairs \((m, n)\) are \((24, 25),\) \((24, -25),\) \((0, 7),\) \((0, -7).\) That’s \(4\) of them. Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Squaring gives \(n^2 - 49 = m^2,\) so \((n - m)(n + m) = 49\)
\(49\) has few factorizations; also \(m = \sqrt{\cdots} \ge 0,\) while \(n\) may be negative
